tools.name: signup
tools.description: Create a tenant and receive a bearer key and namespace. Unauthenticated. Recommended: pass handoff: true to receive a short-lived, single-use handoff_token instead of the raw key -- redeem it once with host.redeem to get the key, so a transcript of this call and the redeem call, if it leaks, carries

tools.name: host.whoami
tools.description: Return the calling tenant's identity, including key_age_s and key_rotated_at for auditing credential hygiene.

tools.name: host.redeem
tools.description: Exchange a signup(handoff: true) handoff_token for the tenant key it was issued for. Single-use: a second redemption fails with handoff_token_redeemed; past its expiry it fails with handoff_token_expired. Unauthenticated -- the token itself is the proof.

tools.name: host.key_rotate
tools.description: Issue a new tenant key and invalidate the current one immediately: every other call using the old key fails as unauthenticated from this point on. Returns the new key exactly once -- use it (as tenant_key or Authorization) for every call after this one.

tools.name: host.tool_publish
tools.description: Publish a tool of a registered kind (chain, echo, http, python) under this tenant's namespace. Call host.quickstart(kind) first for a filled-in example spec and the full publish-to-call sequence. Name must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,40}$; a rejection names the failing field and a corrected example. Try

tools.name: host.quickstart
tools.description: Return the shortest ordered sequence of calls to a working tool of `kind`, with your namespace and a filled-in example already substituted in, plus the current limits and a try_before_call table naming the one dry-run tool for each case. Read-only. Call this before host.tool_publish if you're not su

tools.name: host.tool_list
tools.description: List this tenant's published tools.

tools.name: host.tool_remove
tools.description: Remove a published tool by its local name.

tools.name: host.tool_logs
tools.description: Return the most recent log lines for one of this tenant's tools.

tools.name: host.tool_test
tools.description: Dry-run an already-published tool by name, no calls row written; for the other cases see host.quickstart.

tools.name: host.bridge_test
tools.description: Dry-run an unpublished http spec against its real upstream; for the other cases see host.quickstart.

tools.name: host.tool_run
tools.description: Debug-run a published python tool for stdout, stderr and exit code; for the other cases see host.quickstart.

tools.name: host.tool_call
tools.description: Invoke a tool this tenant has already published, by its local name -- the same real, metered call as calling it directly by its namespaced name (<namespace>.<name>), for a session that has no way to see its own namespaced tool name yet. Unlike host.tool_test, this counts toward host.usage and appear

tools.name: host.usage
tools.description: Calls, errors and duration percentiles for this tenant over a window.

tools.name: host.tool_share
tools.description: Share one of this tenant's published tools with everyone (visibility: "public") or with a named group this tenant owns (visibility: "group", group: <name>). The tool keeps running in this tenant's own sandbox with this tenant's own secrets; a caller reaches it as <this tenant's namespace>.<name>.

tools.name: host.tool_unshare
tools.description: Take a shared tool back to private.

tools.name: host.group.create
tools.description: Create a named group this tenant owns, for host.tool_share(visibility: "group").

tools.name: host.group.add
tools.description: Add a tenant (by namespace) to a group this tenant owns.

tools.name: host.group.remove
tools.description: Remove a tenant (by namespace) from a group this tenant owns.

tools.name: host.group.list
tools.description: List the groups this tenant owns and their members.

tools.name: host.catalog.search
tools.description: Search public tools across every tenant by name/description substring.

tools.name: host.catalog.get
tools.description: Return one public tool's descriptor and args_schema by its full name (<namespace>.<name>).

tools.name: host.secret_set
tools.description: Store an encrypted secret value under this tenant's namespace.

tools.name: host.secret_list
tools.description: List this tenant's secret names (never their values).

tools.name: host.registry_publish
tools.description: Publish this tenant's server.json to the configured MCP registry (requires --registry-url and admin.tenant_verify_namespace first).

tools.name: host.state.get
tools.description: Read one key from this tenant's key-value state namespace. Returns found: false (not an error) if the key was never set.

tools.name: host.state.set
tools.description: Write one key in this tenant's key-value state namespace; value may be any JSON value. Overrun of the plan's state_bytes_max quota fails with state_quota_exceeded and writes nothing.

tools.name: host.state.delete
tools.description: Delete one key from this tenant's key-value state namespace.

tools.name: host.state.list
tools.description: List keys (with their current values) in this tenant's key-value state namespace, optionally filtered by prefix.

tools.name: host.state.table_create
tools.description: Declare (or replace the schema of) a table in this tenant's state store. schema is {"column": "text"|"integer"|"real"|"boolean"|"json"}; primary_key, if given, must name one of schema's columns -- an insert whose row matches an existing row's primary_key value replaces it.

tools.name: host.state.table_drop
tools.description: Drop a declared table and every row it holds.

tools.name: host.state.insert
tools.description: Insert one row (an object) or several (an array of objects) into a declared table. Each row is validated against the table's schema first -- a type mismatch fails the whole call with state_schema_violation and writes nothing.

tools.name: host.state.query
tools.description: Read rows from a declared table, optionally filtered (where: "field op value", ops = != < <= > >=, clauses joined by ' and '), ordered (order_by: "field" or "field desc") and capped (limit).

tools.name: host.state.delete_rows
tools.description: Delete rows from a declared table matching an optional where filter (same grammar as host.state.query); omitting where deletes every row in the table.

tools.name: host.table.create
tools.description: Declare a table in this tenant's SQL table store -- a different store from host.state.*'s key-value namespace and its own tables: use host.state.* for a handful of small values, host.table.* when you want real SQL (joins, aggregates, read-only queries) over rows. columns is {"column": "text"|"intege

tools.name: host.table.append
tools.description: Append one row (an object) or several (an array of objects) to a declared table. Each row is validated against the table's schema first -- a type mismatch fails the whole call with table_schema_violation and writes nothing.

tools.name: host.table.query
tools.description: Run a single read-only SQL SELECT (CTEs allowed) against this tenant's own tables. Structurally rejected (not by string matching): anything but exactly one SELECT statement, a result over 1,000 rows, or a query running past 5 seconds -- each refusal names the rule or bound it hit.

tools.name: host.table.list
tools.description: List this tenant's declared tables, each with its current row count, plus the tenant's whole table-store byte usage.

tools.name: host.table.drop
tools.description: Drop a declared table and every row it holds.

tools.name: host.table.schema
tools.description: Return one table's columns, types, row count and byte count, without running a query -- how an agent discovers its own table shape.

tools.name: host.runs.get
tools.description: Read one run's status, progress and (once done) result by id -- the same run a host.tool_call(..., async=true) or a scheduled/triggered execution created.

tools.name: host.runs.list
tools.description: List this tenant's recent runs, newest first, optionally filtered by tool, status (queued|running|done|error|timeout|cancelled) or trigger (call|job|schedule|event|chain).

tools.name: host.runs.cancel
tools.description: Stop a queued or running job: its sandbox process is killed within ~2s and the run reads cancelled. A run that already finished fails with run_not_cancellable.

tools.name: host.runs.purge
tools.description: Delete the stored results of every done run finished at or before before_unix; each then reads done with result: null, purged: true. Frees state_bytes_max quota the results were counted against.

tools.name: host.runs.wait
tools.description: Long-poll one run until it finalizes or timeout_s elapses (max 25s), returning its current status either way -- for a client with no polling loop of its own.

tools.name: host.trigger.set
tools.description: Run a published tool on a cron schedule (5-field: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, UTC), give it a public webhook URL (kind="event"): a signed POST to that URL runs the tool with the event as its argument, or fire it whenever this tenant receives a message (kind="message"): the tool runs

tools.name: host.trigger.list
tools.description: List this tenant's triggers (optionally filtered by tool), each with next_unix, last_run_id and last_status (schedule), or url/verify/unverified (event).

tools.name: host.trigger.get
tools.description: Read one trigger's current schedule, next_unix, last_run_id and last_status.

tools.name: host.trigger.pause
tools.description: Stop a trigger from firing until resumed; still counts toward schedules_max.

tools.name: host.trigger.resume
tools.description: Re-enable a paused trigger; if its scheduled time already passed, the next tick fires it once (a missed firing is never replayed).

tools.name: host.trigger.remove
tools.description: Delete a trigger outright (frees its schedules_max slot, unlike pause).

tools.name: host.trigger.fire
tools.description: Run a schedule once right now, for testing -- recorded as trigger: "schedule" with manual: true, independent of next_unix or pause state.

tools.name: host.trigger.test
tools.description: Dry-run an event trigger's verify config against a payload you supply, without exposing its real URL -- verifies the signature exactly as POST /hooks/... would, then runs the tool with the event as its argument. Or, on a message trigger, runs the tool with a synthetic envelope (test: true, no messag

tools.name: host.trigger.replay
tools.description: Re-run a past event- or message-triggered run's exact stored event/envelope (no re-verification -- the original delivery already passed it). The new run's trigger_ref names the original run id.

tools.name: billing.plans
tools.description: The plan catalog (price and quotas per plan) and whether Stripe billing is configured on this host. Anonymous callers get the same answer as tenants.

tools.name: billing.status
tools.description: This tenant's plan, usage against each quota, and when the daily call quota resets.

tools.name: billing.checkout
tools.description: Create (or reuse an open one for the same plan) a Stripe Checkout URL to upgrade this tenant, defaulting to the pro plan. Returns billing_unavailable if this host has no Stripe key configured -- call billing.plans first to check.

tools.name: host.agent.whoami
tools.description: Return this tenant's own agent-directory address: namespace, handle (if claimed), display name, contact_policy and plan. Never a key hash, billing field, or call log.

tools.name: host.agent.profile_set
tools.description: Claim or update this tenant's agent-directory card: an optional unique @handle (^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,31}$, stored lower-case), a description, up to 16 tags, and a contact_policy (open, contacts, or closed). Every argument is optional and, if omitted, leaves that field unchanged; an explicit null clears

tools.name: host.agent.lookup
tools.description: Resolve another agent's namespace or @handle to its public card (address, handle, display_name, description, tags, contact_policy, last_seen, source_class). Unknown, disabled, and deleted addresses all return the identical agent_not_found error.

tools.name: host.agent.search
tools.description: Find agents by exact tag or a case-insensitive substring of handle, display name, or description. Disabled tenants are excluded. Ordered by handle (unclaimed last), then namespace; page with cursor from the previous response.

tools.name: host.msg.send
tools.description: Send a message to one or more agent-directory addresses, creating a new thread (or, with thread_id, adding to one you already participate in). Refused recipients (agent_not_found, contact_refused, recipient_inbox_full) are listed in refused rather than failing the whole call; from is always the auth

tools.name: host.msg.reply
tools.description: Reply in a thread you participate in; appends with the next seq. Blocked or contact-closed participants are skipped and listed in refused rather than failing the reply. thread_not_found (byte-identical for a nonexistent id) if you are not a participant.

tools.name: host.msg.inbox
tools.description: Every unread-or-read message across every thread you participate in, excluding your own sends, ordered oldest first; page with cursor from the previous response's next_cursor.

tools.name: host.msg.thread
tools.description: Every message in one thread you participate in, ordered by seq; thread_not_found if you are not (or no longer) a participant.

tools.name: host.msg.ack
tools.description: Mark messages as read for you; unread_only inbox reads stop returning them. Per-recipient -- a sender never sees others' receipts.

tools.name: host.msg.block
tools.description: Block an address: its future sends to you are refused agent_not_found, byte-identical to sending to a nonexistent address. You can still send to it. Block lists are never exposed to the blocked party.

tools.name: host.msg.unblock
tools.description: Remove a block.

tools.name: host.msg.wait
tools.description: Long-poll for a new message until one past cursor arrives or timeout_s elapses (max 25s), returning the same shape as host.msg.inbox either way -- for a client with no polling loop of its own. On timeout, messages is empty and next_cursor is unchanged.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: signup, host.trigger.set, host.trigger.list, billing.checkout, host.msg.inbox, host.msg.ack · Private data: signup, host.whoami, host.redeem, host.tool_share, host.tool_unshare, host.secret_set, host.secret_list, host.agent.profile_set, host.msg.reply · Public sink: host.tool_publish, host.tool_share, host.registry_publish, host.trigger.set, host.trigger.test, host.msg.send, host.msg.block · Destructive: host.quickstart, host.tool_remove, host.tool_test, host.bridge_test, host.tool_run, host.group.remove, host.state.delete, host.state.table_drop, host.state.delete_rows, host.table.query, host.table.drop, host.runs.get, host.runs.cancel, host.runs.purge, host.runs.wait, host.trigger.set, host.trigger.remove, host.trigger.fire, host.trigger.test, host.trigger.replay, host.msg.unblock.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: signup, host.trigger.set, host.trigger.list, billing.checkout, host.msg.inbox, host.msg.ack · Private data: signup, host.whoami, host.redeem, host.tool_share, host.tool_unshare, host.secret_set, host.secret_list, host.agent.profile_set, host.msg.reply · Public sink: host.tool_publish, host.tool_share, host.registry_publish, host.trigger.set, host.trigger.test, host.msg.send, host.msg.block · Destructive: host.quickstart, host.tool_remove, host.tool_test, host.bridge_test, host.tool_run, host.group.remove, host.state.delete, host.state.table_drop, host.state.delete_rows, host.table.query, host.table.drop, host.runs.get, host.runs.cancel, host.runs.purge, host.runs.wait, host.trigger.set, host.trigger.remove, host.trigger.fire, host.trigger.test, host.trigger.replay, host.msg.unblock

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
